subject: Red team scope: hosting variant inclusion & exclusions (requested evidence & remediation cadence)
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hillcresthealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@hillcresthealth.com
Date: 2025-06-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Red team scoping question: hosting variants

Priya / team,

Thanks for taking this — Hillcrest is preparing for our annual red-team engagement and we want to confirm exactly which Redwood-managed components will be in scope. The engagement team asked us to clarify three specific items: Hosted (Redwood hosted API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private/VPC (customer VPC & on-prem package).

We need two things from you before the intake on Tuesday: 1) a short list that says "Included" vs "Excluded" for each deployment variant and a one-line justification, and 2) any supporting artifacts (asset inventory, network segmentation diagram) you can share ahead of the test.

Can you also confirm typical remediation SLAs you accept for critical/high findings and whether you offer a separate window for customer-managed Private deployments?

I've attached the Hillcrest intake questionnaire we usually send to vendors (redteam-questionnaire.pdf). Intake call scheduled: 2025-06-17 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Sam Ortega
Security Program Manager
Hillcrest Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hillcresthealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Red team scoping question: hosting variants

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the questionnaire. High-level answers below; attaching a short coverage matrix and our asset inventory for the in-scope systems (hosting-coverage-matrix-20250614.xlsx, asset-inventory-redteam.csv).

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): INCLUDED — our hosted inference runtime and public API endpoints are in-scope. We exclude cloud provider-managed control-plane features that are not part of our runtime (e.g., underlying host hypervisor operations).
- Dedicated (Reserved GPU pools): INCLUDED — Dedicated capacity nodes, our orchestration, autoscaler, scheduling, and model runtime are in-scope. Any customer-managed VPC peering endpoints and customer-owned data stores are OUT-OF-SCOPE unless we have a signed statement of work to include them.
- Private / VPC (customer VPC or on‑prem): PARTIAL — Redwood-managed components that we deploy into customer environments (our runtime binaries and control-plane agents we operate) are INCLUDED. Customer-managed services (KMS keys, databases, identity providers inside the VPC/on-prem) are OUT-OF-SCOPE by default. For on-prem installs where Redwood provides an appliance and manages the whole stack under contract, that installation can be IN-SCOPE if the customer requests Redwood to authorize the test and provides network access for testers.

Remediation cadence:
- Critical findings: 7 calendar days to provide a mitigation plan; 30 calendar days to complete remediation, unless an exception is mutually agreed.
- High findings: 14 calendar days to provide remediation plan; 60 calendar days to remediate.
- Exceptions: Private/on‑prem systems may have different windows depending on the customer's change control processes; we handle on a per-customer basis.

Pre-engagement items we can share today: asset inventory, host list, architecture diagrams. We cannot share customer-owned keys or any PII-containing logs without an executed DPA and approved red-team NDA.

Owners: 
- Scope and artifacts: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.ai)
- Remediation tracking: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai)
- Technical contact for private installs: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.ai)

I'll upload the matrix and inventory to the drive link and bring the detailed matrix to the intake call. If Hillcrest needs us to bring a specific test plan for dedicated vs private, let us know ahead of the call.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hillcresthealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@hillcresthealth.com
Date: 2025-06-17T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Red team scoping question: hosting variants

Priya / Marcus — thanks for the matrix on the call. A couple of clarifications that came up from the red-team vendor: 

1) Dedicated + VPC peering: the red team wants to know if peer connections (network routes from Hillcrest VPC to Dedicated nodes) will be test targets or if those peering endpoints are considered customer-only.
2) Private installs: we heard that Redwood-managed agents running in-customer are included; can you confirm whether agent-to-control-plane traffic (mTLS endpoints) is part of scope?

Hillcrest will need evidence artifacts for our SOC 2 binder: the network segmentation diagram and proof that tenant-sidecar containers are excluded (or documented) from test scope. Also please indicate whether the remediation tracker will be shared back to Hillcrest once issues are closed.

We need those artifacts before the vendor kickoff (planned for 2025-06-24). Thanks — Sam

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hillcresthealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Red team scoping question: hosting variants

Sam — quick status update and attachments.

Answers to your clarifications: 
- Dedicated + VPC peering: PEER ENDPOINTS are treated as CUSTOMER-BOUNDARY by default. The dedicated node interfaces managed by Redwood (our agent and orchestration endpoints) are in-scope; the peering link and customer network appliances are out-of-scope unless Hillcrest explicitly asks to include them and signs a statement of work. We've documented this in the attached scope statement (redteam-20250624-scope-statement.pdf).
- Agent <-> control-plane mTLS traffic: INCLUDED — we consider the agent channels part of the runtime and allow red-team testing of the mTLS endpoints we manage. We do not provide private key material; tests should not attempt to exfiltrate customer-managed KMS material.

Artifacts attached here: network-segmentation-diagram.png, hosting-coverage-matrix-20250614.xlsx, asset-inventory-redteam.csv, redteam-20250624-scope-statement.pdf.

Remediation & evidence sharing: 
- We will provide Hillcrest a read-only remediation tracker that contains issue IDs, severity, remediation status, and close dates. Laura will coordinate exports for your SOC 2 binder.
- Expected timeline: vendor kickoff 2025-06-24; initial findings delivered within 14 days post-test; final report + remediation evidence within 45 days.

Exceptions: for Private/on-prem installations where Hillcrest owns the network segment and change control, we require Hillcrest to accept different operational timelines; we'll call these out on the SOW.

I'll send the Drive link and upload the artifacts now (also sending redteam-engagement-order.pdf for the vendor). Marcus / Laura — please confirm you uploaded the CSV and matrix and that Laura can export the tracker for Hillcrest.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-segmentation-diagram.png; hosting-coverage-matrix-20250614.xlsx; asset-inventory-redteam.csv; redteam-20250624-scope-statement.pdf; redteam-engagement-order.pdf
